_README: The offices this site does not track the votes of: the Governor, the five
Executive Councillors, the two members of the US House and the two US
Senators. None of them appear in any General Court file, which is where
everything else on Granite Record comes from.
THIS FILE IS EDITED BY HAND AND NO GENERATOR WRITES IT, for the same
reason ground_truth.csv is: a name against an office is a claim about a
real person holding real power, and it must come from somebody who
checked rather than from a build step that guessed.
Every record carries the page it was read from and the date it was read.
These offices change at an election; when one does, the names here are
stale and the official_url is still right, which is why the page links to
it either way.
PARTY IS RECORDED ONLY WHERE A SOURCE STATED IT, AND THE SOURCE IS NAMED.
senate.gov gives a party for each senator. governor.nh.gov,
council.nh.gov and the members' own house.gov sites do not, so those
eight were blank until 12 September 2026, when the site's author
supplied them: Ayotte R, Kenney R, Liot Hill D, Stevens R, Stephen R,
Wheeler R, Pappas D, Goodlander D. That is a person's statement rather
than a page's, which is the whole reason this file is a person's file.
A party chip is a visible claim about a real person; if one of these is
wrong, it is wrong here and nowhere else.

governor.name: Kelly Ayotte
about: As the head of state government, the Governor signs or vetoes legislation passed in the General Court, oversees state agencies, and proposes the state budget for legislative approval.
Five councilors, elected from five districts. The Executive Council approves state contracts over $10,000, judicial and agency nominations, and pardons.
New Hampshire elects two members of the US House, one from each congressional district.
us_house.source: https://www.sos.nh.gov/congressional-delegation, and each member's own site for the district
